purpose: Freeze the coordinate-capacity lemma discovered while following uniquely-decodable two-codebook / multiple-access-channel literature. This is theorem-side research only.

definitions.cross_compatible: For every p in P and q in Q, no coordinate contains opposite nonzero signs POS/NEG across the pair.
definitions.injective_signed_union: All coordinatewise compatible unions p union q are pairwise distinct over P x Q.
definitions.P_private_ternary_coordinate: P uses both POS and NEG at the coordinate; cross-compatibility then forces Q to be constantly OMIT there.
definitions.Q_private_ternary_coordinate: Q uses both POS and NEG; P is constantly OMIT there.
definitions.shared_binary_coordinate: Neither side uses both signs; cross-compatibility permits at most one common nonzero sign plus OMIT, so the coordinate behaves as at most a binary OR output.

lemma.statement: Let P,Q be a complete cross-compatible injective signed-union code pair on r coordinates. If e_P coordinates are P-private ternary, e_Q are Q-private ternary, and s=r-e_P-e_Q are the remaining at-most-binary coordinates, then |P|<=3^e_P*2^s, |Q|<=3^e_Q*2^s, and |P||Q|<=3^(e_P+e_Q)*2^s. Consequently a candidate pair (|P|,|Q|) is impossible whenever no nonnegative integer triple (e_P,e_Q,s) summing to r satisfies all three inequalities.
proof_sketch: Cross-compatibility yields the three coordinate types by inspecting the projections of P and Q onto one coordinate.
P is constant OMIT on every Q-private coordinate, has at most three symbols on each P-private coordinate, and at most two on each shared coordinate, so |P|<=3^e_P*2^s. Symmetrically for Q.

The union output itself has at most three values on a private coordinate and two on a shared coordinate; global injectivity therefore gives |P||Q| no larger than the output alphabet product 3^(e_P+e_Q)*2^s.

N58_neighbor_equality_application.historical_existing_algorithmist_equalit: To attain the inherited raw_units=3365 ceiling, every one of pq=609 cross-parent pairs had to produce a new distinct non-tautological resolvent.
application: 609 distinct outputs require 3^(e_P+e_Q)*2^s >=609. For r=6, five ternary coordinates and one binary coordinate give only 3^5*2=486, so all six coordinates must be private ternary: s=0 and e_P+e_Q=6.
N58_neighbor_equality_application.relation_to_existing_algorithmist_proof: Independent shorter channel-capacity proof of the same equality-case impossibility already frozen by Algorithmist at commit a09b5fca8b3acc29f3423c56fb70e2544814f66d. No claim of priority/novelty is made.

N58_22x22_application.source: The separate injective-rectangle bridge from historical J>=610 extracts a 22x22 complete injective rectangle.
N58_22x22_application.result: 484 outputs force at least five private ternary coordinates because 3^4*2^2=324<484. Five are impossible since both 22-word codebooks require at least three private ternary coordinates when only one shared binary coordinate remains. Therefore the rectangle must have all six coordinates private, split exactly 3+3. The omission-mass handoff then gives 164>162 and closes the case.

literature_context.primary: T. Kasami, S. Lin, Coding for a Multiple-Access Channel
literature_context.connection: Exact two-codebook deterministic coordinate channel with global unique decodability.

literature_context.primary: P. Vanroose, Code construction for the noiseless binary switching multiple-access channel
literature_context.connection: Two-codebook zero-error capacity/finite code-pair bounds for another deterministic binary-input MAC; reinforces treating coordinate-channel type as a first-class structural resource.

literature_context.connection: General symmetric f-MAC and almost-separable language; inspired the output-alphabet decomposition but its published numeric bounds are not used here.
